item.name: LionDriver Level 2 Driver Assistance Platform
item.author: Jherrod Thomas (FSM); drafted with Claude Code
item.approver: Pending independent confirmation review (safety plan anomaly A01)

hazards.H01: Unintended lateral motion (steering too much, too fast, in the wrong direction, or uncommanded)
hazards.H02: Loss or weakness of lateral control while the driver relies on it
hazards.H04: Unintended or excessive deceleration that exposes the vehicle to a rear-end collision
hazards.H05: Insufficient deceleration when braking is needed
hazards.H06: Failure to release control when the driver brakes, cancels or overrides
hazards.H07: Engagement of control without a deliberate driver action
hazards.H09: Driver unawareness of the system state (believing it controls when it does not, or missing a take-over request)

safe_states.F01: Lateral control off: the panda blocks all steering commands and the stock steering returns full authority to the driver; audible take-over alert.
safe_states.F02: Longitudinal control off: no acceleration or braking request; the vehicle returns to driver control of speed; audible take-over alert.
safe_states.F03: Controls not allowed: the panda blocks every actuator command until the driver engages again.
safe_states.F04: Escalate to disengagement with an audible alert; engagement unavailable until monitoring is healthy.
safe_states.F06: Disengage with an audible alert when the displayed state cannot be guaranteed.

environments.rationale: Off-road (L06) and snow or ice (W05) are outside the operating envelope (assumption A01 of LD-ITD-001). Fog is kept: it is outside the validated conditions but a driver can foreseeably keep the system engaged in it.

function_malfunction_ratings.rationale: Lateral control engaged but no steering output: vehicle drifts out of lane if the driver relies on it.
Steering assistance stops mid-curve while engaged.
Steering command while not engaged or not needed: unexpected lateral motion.
Steering command held at last value: vehicle keeps turning after the road straightens.
Steering command larger than needed: lane departure toward adjacent traffic or road edge.
Steering too weak to follow the curve.
Steering into a curve before it starts is unrequested lateral motion.
Steering into a curve too late behaves as insufficient steering.
Assistance that ends too soon behaves as stops functioning.
Steering that continues too long behaves as stuck.
Delayed steering behaves as insufficient steering at the moment it is needed.
Steering in the wrong direction: the most adversarial lateral failure.
Oscillating steering: weaving within or out of the lane.
Asymmetric steering (pulling one way) behaves as excessive steering in that direction.
ACC engaged but no deceleration for a slower lead vehicle.
Longitudinal control stops while following: loss of braking for the lead vehicle.
Acceleration request without need: unintended acceleration (unintended braking is covered under M07).
Request held at last value: continued acceleration toward the lead vehicle (stuck braking is covered under M10).
Acceleration greater than needed (excessive braking is covered under M07).
Braking weaker than needed to keep distance.
Braking before it is needed, or with no reason: phantom braking.
Braking that starts too late behaves as insufficient deceleration.
Braking that ends too soon behaves as stops functioning.
Braking that continues too long: the vehicle slows or stops in traffic unexpectedly.
Delayed braking behaves as late braking.
Accelerating when braking is needed.
Alternating acceleration and braking; the braking pulses are the governing hazard for following traffic.
Single-axis output: unevenness is not a distinct failure mode.
Disengagement fails: the system keeps control while the driver brakes or cancels and fights the driver.
Engagement management stops working while engaged: control can no longer be released.
Engagement without a driver action: steering and speed control start unexpectedly.
Engagement state stuck at engaged.
No magnitude: engagement is a discrete state.
No magnitude: engagement is a discrete state.
Engaging before the driver's action completes is unrequested engagement.
Control released late after a brake press: the system holds authority while the driver reacts.
Engagement lasting too short is an unexpected disengagement, analyzed as F01/F02 M02 (stops functioning).
Staying engaged too long behaves as failure to disengage.
Delayed release behaves as late release.
Engaging on a disengage action (for example a brake press).
Flapping between engaged and disengaged: repeated unexpected engagement.
Not applicable to a discrete state.
Monitoring fails: an inattentive driver is neither warned nor disengaged.
Monitoring stops during a drive.
False inattention alerts are a nuisance; a resulting disengagement is analyzed as F01/F02 M02.
Attention estimate stuck at attentive.
Over-sensitive monitoring gives early warnings: nuisance, not a hazard.
Monitoring detects only some inattention.
Early warnings: nuisance, not a hazard.
Warnings come too late for an inattentive driver to recover.
Warnings too short are covered by escalation to disengagement.
Warnings too long: nuisance.
Delayed warnings behave as late warnings.
Inverse estimate (attentive driver flagged, inattentive one not) contains the M01 hazard.
Intermittent alerts: nuisance; persistent failure is M01.
Not applicable.

rating_rules.rationale: C2. Loss or weakness of assistance, not an adversarial input. Under assumption A03 the supervising driver's hands and feet are available and the vehicle continues on its current path, so 90% or more of drivers are expected to correct. Key review item: C1 is arguable for a supervised Level 2 system; C3 if foreseeable over-reliance (A04) is weighted.
Severity of the eventual unhandled event, for example an unnoticed lane departure, at the location's speed band.

E2. The operational situation is the combination of an inattentive driver and a situation the system does not handle, while monitoring has failed. Rated on the situation's duration share, not on the monitoring failure rate.
C3. By definition the driver is inattentive and unwarned.
Severity of a lane departure or late take-over at the location's speed band.
E3. Situations where the driver depends on the displayed state (curves, take-over requests) occur regularly while driving with the system.
C2. The vehicle's own behavior (drift, no steering feel) gives the driver a cue within seconds.
